item.title: AFK 0.5.1
item.description:
Your earbuds and AFK get along now

If you held the key right after your AirPods or other Bluetooth earbuds connected, AFK could crash. Sorry about that. Bluetooth mics change how they send audio the moment they connect, and AFK kept listening the old way. Now it keeps up: switch mics whenever you like, even halfway through a dictation, and the recording carries on.

One honest catch: on Bluetooth there's a short pause between holding the key and AFK hearing you, because macOS first flips your earbuds into call mode. Start talking a beat later and you won't lose a word. Wired earphones and your Mac's own mic don't have the pause.

Also fixed and added

  • No more pasting your previous dictation. When an app was busy, it sometimes pasted the dictation before last instead of the one you just said. AFK now waits until the app has actually taken your text before it puts your clipboard back, and it puts all of it back, images and files included.
  • A failed transcription isn't lost anymore. AFK keeps the audio of each dictation on your Mac for 24 hours, then deletes it. If one fails, it's waiting at the top of Notes with a Try again button. Clear it any time in Settings → Data.
  • The recording waveform starts flat every time, and keeps pace on Bluetooth mics.
  • The sidebar icons lost their blue.
  • Questions, problems or ideas? My email is now in Settings → About: keshavatearth@gmail.com. I read every one.

Keshav

item.title: AFK 0.5.0
item.description:
AFK can transcribe videos now

  • Drop MP4, MOV or M4V videos into Transcribe: screen recordings, iPhone videos, Zoom and Loom downloads. AFK transcribes the video's audio on your Mac.

Smaller improvements

  • Save finished transcripts to a folder automatically, as TXT, SRT or JSON. Existing files are never overwritten.
  • A smaller recording indicator, in Settings → Dictation, with both sizes shown side by side.
  • If part of a long file can't be transcribed, AFK keeps the rest and tells you which part is missing, instead of skipping it silently.
  • The Delete all history confirmation now says exactly what it removes.
  • The bundled Agent Skill covers video files.

item.title: AFK 0.4.3
item.description:
Choose your dictation shortcuts

  • Configure the hold-to-dictate key and the hands-free start and stop sequences.
  • Shortcut fields update every instruction in AFK and include one-click restore defaults.
  • The default shortcuts remain Right Option, Right Option + A-F-K, and Right Option + Return.

item.title: AFK 0.4.2
item.description:
Tell me what to build next

  • New menu item: “Request a Feature…” — opens the public ⌥AFK feature board, where you can post an idea or vote on someone else’s. No account, no email required, same as the app itself. What gets voted up is what I build next.
  • The board also carries a roadmap and a changelog, so you can see what’s in flight.

item.title: AFK 0.4.1
item.description:
Stability release — nine fixes from real crash reports

  • Fixed the hotkey crash. A mic hiccup (AirPods switching, waking from sleep) could make every following dictation attempt crash the app until relaunch. Crash reports from the field confirmed it; it's gone. Failures now show a message with what to do instead.
  • The recording pill is reliable on fast back-to-back dictations — stale hide animations can no longer make it invisible mid-recording.
  • Filler-word removal is on by default (it was accidentally off for fresh installs). Conservative list: um, uh, hmm and friends — never real words. If you'd turned it off, your choice stands.
  • Long file transcriptions can't be lost at the finish line — a sliver-length final chunk or one bad patch of audio no longer throws away hours of finished text.
  • Dictation history is safer: saves moved off the UI thread, and a corrupt file now heals (with a backup) instead of silently wiping your archive.
  • Dictionary entries now replace whole words only — "cat → Kat" no longer turns "category" into "Kategory".
  • A busy or frozen app can no longer stall the hotkey listener while AFK asks it where to type.

item.title: AFK 0.4.0
item.description:
Transcriptions that survive, and a language picker

  • File transcriptions keep running when you switch tabs or close the window — with a real progress bar. Finished results stick around for an hour (even across a relaunch) so you can't lose one by clicking away.
  • Save to keep — saving a transcript records it in History's new Files tab (where it went, how long the audio was, how fast it transcribed). AFK never stores the transcript text itself; unsaved results expire after an hour.
  • Default language — pick your dictation language in Settings (English by default). This also fixes the rare case where English speech came out in Cyrillic. Applies instantly, no relaunch.
  • CLI: afk transcribe file.mp3 --lang en.
  • "Delete all history" now asks first — and never cancels a transcription in progress.

item.title: AFK 0.3.0
item.description:
Word-level timestamps + shareable scoreboard

  • Timestamps view on file transcripts — toggle to see every segment with mm:ss times.
  • Export as .srt or .json from the Save menu (subtitles, video editing, or your own scripts). Also in the CLI: afk transcribe file --srt | --json.
  • Share card — one click on Home renders your dictation scoreboard (words, time saved, WPM, rank) as an image, saved to Downloads and copied to the clipboard.
